messages:
maria: FYI an enterprise customer escalated — big p95/p99 latency spike starting ~08:15 UTC after we promoted tool-calling + structured output validation to default. They reported timeouts and increased error budgets.

raj: ack. can you paste the example request?

maria: root payload (redacted) -> they use tool router + strict JSON schema validation on outputs. quick repro we received from them:
```
POST /v1/generate
Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "model": "redwood-qa-3b",
  "input": "Summarize 2000 rows of transaction data with tool calls",
  "tool_calls": true,
  "structured_output": {"schema": {"type":"object","properties":{...},"required":[...]}}
  ,"stream": false
}
```

maria: their p50 is fine, p95 jumped from ~180ms to ~420ms, p99 from ~520ms to ~1.2s after enabling strict schema checks and tool router.

samira: any traces? can we see a span breakdown?

raj: pulled a few traces from their tenant id. short summary from one slow request:
```
span: request-entry (12ms)
span: auth (3ms)
span: router-tool-selection (75ms)
span: model-inference (220ms)
span: schema-validator (480ms)
span: tool-router-io (110ms)
span: response-aggregation (10ms)
```

raj: schema-validator is the big tail contributor on that sample. validator runs JSON schema $ref resolution + deep validation for nested arrays.

eli: sounds like worst-case O(n) validation on large outputs. we probably don't stream-validate; we validate synchronously after generation finishes -> long tail.

alex: customer says it only started after they flipped "structured_output.strict": true in their app. before that they were using a looser schema.

maria: they attached logs showing many validator worker queue waits around the same time (queue depth spike).

samira: immediate mitigations we can do now: 1) flip strict validation off per-tenant via feature flag; 2) add temporary validator concurrency increase for that tenant; 3) route that tenant to a fast-path that skips heavy $ref resolution.

raj: implemented a hotfix branch to short-circuit $ref resolution if schema size > 8KB and fallen back to shallow type checks. will canary to 10% traffic for Tenant X.

deploy-bot: deploy started: hotfix/fast-validator -> canary(10%) -> prod.

raj: quick perf note — shallow checks cut validator time from ~480ms to ~35-60ms in our bench.

maria: customer on phone wants ETA. we told them a canary in next 15m and monitoring for 30m after.

alex: monitoring dashboard pinned: support/p95-tenantX, p99-tenantX, validator-queue-depth. I'll watch.

samira: medium-term fixes we should track: 1) move validation to validator worker pool (async) with streaming feedback and best-effort failure mode; 2) cache compiled schemas per-tenant and share compiled validators; 3) add size/complexity-based policy that defaults to lightweight checks; 4) expose diagnostic header X-RW-Validator-Duration.

eli: additional idea: for tool-calling path, validate tool output per-tool (smaller schemas) instead of validating entire final aggregated object. reduces surface area.

raj: agreed. also add circuit-breaker: if validator queue depth > 200 or median > 200ms, auto-disable strict mode for that tenant and emit audit log.

maria: reproducible steps for eng to validate locally (provided to customer as well):
```
# run local server with sample schema
python -m rwdev run --tenant test-tenant --enable-tool-router --enable-structured-output
# send payload (fast loop to emulate load)
for i in {1..200}; do \
curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8080/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer test' \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-qa-3b","input":"...","tool_calls":true,"structured_output":{"schema":<big-schema>}}' &\
done
```

raj: repro succeeded locally, saw same queueing. I'll attach flamegraphs to the ticket.

samira: owners: raj -> short-term hotfix & circuit-breaker; eli -> schema compile/cache design; alex -> monitoring/SLIs and customer comms; maria -> primary support contact.

maria: customer pleased with canary plan, asked for rollback plan if anything breaks.

raj: rollback: revert feature flag to previous state (strict off) for that tenant; deploy rollback script ready.

deploy-bot: canary deployed successfully (10%). metrics: validator median 42ms, p95 reduced to 210ms for canary traffic.

alex: p99 for canary still ~320ms but overall much better than 1.2s. keeping on watch for 30m.

maria: asking customer for confirmation to widen to 50%.

customer (via support DM pasted by maria): "thank you — we're seeing big improvement. will wait 30m and thumbs up to widen."

samira: follow-ups (tickets/tasks):
- T1: ship async validator worker + streaming validation (owner: raj, ETA: 2w)
- T2: schema compiled cache + complexity heuristics (owner: eli, ETA: 1w)
- T3: expose validator latency headers + tenant-level feature flags (owner: alex, ETA: 3d)
- T4: add router tool-call per-tool validation optimization (owner: eli, ETA: 2w)

raj: I'll attach a short postmortem draft after 48h with root cause (sync heavy validation + queueing) and mitigations.

maria: thanks team. will update customer and mark incident as 'escalation — mitigation in progress'. :thumbsup:

alex: cpu/mem on validator nodes had headroom but lock contention on schema compile was visible. repeated compile of large schemas is a real perf bug. cache wins are huge.

eli: noted — will prototype a shared compiled-schema cache (LRU) with TTL and store a schema-hash in tenant config.

samira: tagging infra for capacity planning if we need to scale validator pool (cc @infra).

maria: closing loop after widen to 50% and 2h of stable metrics. will reopen if regressions.

raj: attaching sample trace id for postmortem: trace-0x7f9a12b3.

deploy-bot: canary -> 50% rollout started.

maria: customer confirmed improvement after 50% rollout. final notes: recommend customers keep strict validation opt-in until we ship async validator.

samira: thanks all. good triage.
